messages:
alex.kim: FYI customer (acct: acme-payments) hit a reproducible case where streaming tool-call args get cut off when requests flow through their auth proxy. Their app sees a malformed JSON payload and our function/charge tool errors out.

maria.gupta: Can you paste the minimal repro and any proxy config? Also, which SDK/path are they using (chat.stream / sse)?

alex.kim: Using chat streaming (SSE) to our hosted API from a server behind an auth proxy that does an upstream auth_request (nginx). Repro steps below. Happens ~30% of streams.

alex.kim: Repro (simplified):
```bash
# client -> nginx auth proxy -> internet -> redwood hosted API (SSE)
curl -N -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"charge order 98765 amount 100"}],"functions":[{"name":"charge","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"integer"},"amount":{"type":"number"}},"required":["order_id","amount"]}}],"function_call":{"name":"charge"}}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```

alex.kim: Server-side log from client after the stream: we get SSE chunks like: ``event: message
data: {\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"name\":\"charge\",\"args\":{\"order_id\":98765,\"amount\":10`` (last chunk ends mid-number). Our parser treats each SSE data block as a complete JSON and fails with parse error.

kevin_h: Do we reassemble across SSE chunks today? I thought the client SDK concatenates data events before JSON.parse. If they're using raw curl it might behave differently.

maria.gupta: Our runtime emits chunks as we generate tokens; SSE "data:" lines can be split arbitrarily by proxies. SDKs are usually resilient, but server-side proxies can also split inside the JSON text. We should not rely on one SSE "data" containing a whole JSON.

support_lead: Customer says their app (node fetch) hits JSON.parse on each data event. They can't change upstream immediately. We need mitigation + root cause.

alex.kim: Quick mitigation we suggested to customer: buffer SSE data events on their side and only JSON.parse when complete object (match braces) OR use our SDK which does reassembly. They need steps they can apply server-side (nginx) too.

maria.gupta: On nginx auth proxy, common culprits: 
- proxy_request_buffering on (can change chunking)
- gzip / deflate altering chunk boundaries
- any sub-filter that re-encodes response body
Recommend setting: 
```
proxy_request_buffering off;
proxy_buffering off;
gzip off;
proxy_set_header Connection "keep-alive";
```
These reduce rewriting/fragmentation.

kevin_h: Filed an eng-runtime ticket for SDK/server-side reassembly and to make SSE data concatenation explicit in docs. Ticket: RWINF-8642 (pinged eng-runtime).

sre-bot: [incident-log] 2312345689: stream-json-parse-errors spike (acme-payments) 14 errors in 10m, backoff triggered for that key.

alex.kim: Customer asked if we can make the runtime emit an explicit boundary marker per JSON payload (e.g., a newline delimiter) to reduce fragility. Thoughts?

maria.gupta: We can consider adding an optional framing mode: NDJSON (\n-delimited) or boundary token. Backwards compatibility concerns though. Short-term: docs + SDK fixes + suggest proxy settings. Long-term: add framing flag on streaming endpoints.

support_lead: Action items:
1) Share nginx config snippet with customer (maria) ✅
2) Provide minimal client-side buffer example (alex) ✅
3) Eng ticket for SDK + framing options (kevin) -> RWINF-8642 ✅
4) Ask customer for proxy logs/pcap for one repro run (alex)

alex.kim: Sending proxy logs to secure-share now. Will follow up with repro pcap and exact request ids. Thanks team :pray:

kevin_h: I'll prioritize RWINF-8642 and scope prototype for NDJSON framing. If we need to hotfix SDK quick, we can push a patch to node-fetch wrapper this week.

maria.gupta: Noted. I'll draft a KB article for support with examples on how to safely parse SSE streaming tool calls when proxies are in path.

support_lead: Thanks — keep me posted. :thumbsup:
